label: PF Backlog 187
title: Backend: split backlog storage into per-item files (truth) + DERIVED index + content journal (one-time change)
body:
## Problem / why
The backlog keeps ALL items in one array file (`open.json` / `closed.json`) and rewrites the whole
file on every change (`core/backlog.py:_wj`). Per-item `history/<ID>.jsonl` records STATUS only,
not content. There is no lean tracker view; the array is truth AND the detail store at once.

## Goal & value
Split "tracking" from "detail", ONCE, in a single change:
- index (`open.json`/`index.json`) = id, status, one-liner, created/updated (tracking/journal view);
- per-item file = the FULL item (today's rich format);
- per-item `history/<ID>.jsonl` = a CONTENT journal (title/body/link before -> after), not status only.
Value: smaller diffs, O(1) writes, real per-item history, a clean tracker view. Internal only.

## In scope
- Stage 1 (low risk): enrich `history/<ID>.jsonl` to a content journal AND generate a compact DERIVED
  `index.json` (id, status, one-liner, created_at, updated_at) beside the existing `index.html`.
- Stage 2 (structural): per-item files `items/<ID>.json` become the TRUTH; `open.json`/`index.json`
  become DERIVED (regenerated), never hand-edited.
- Single-source migration of all existing items + journals; keep a read-fallback for the old layout.

## Out of scope
- Any change to item SEMANTICS (fields, statuses, ids, links) or to the backlog API signatures.
- The dashboard UI; other stores (intake `items.jsonl`, events) - only referenced for consistency.

## Flow
1. Writer updates the per-item file (truth) + appends the content journal.
2. Writer regenerates the derived index (id/status/one-liner/dates).
3. Readers use the SAME API (`list_open`, `get_by_ref`, `update`) - unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- Given the refactor, all existing items/journals migrate with ZERO data loss (count + content hashes match).
- Given a change to an item, only that item's file + the derived index change (O(1) diff).
- Given any consumer, behaviour is identical (same API, same results) - no code changes outside
  `core/backlog.py` (+ migration + views/audit).
- Given the old layout still present, a read-fallback works (no hard cutover).

## Data model (what is stored, where, owner)
- `items/<ID>.json` = full item (truth) · `history/<ID>.jsonl` = content+status journal ·
  `open.json`/`index.json` = DERIVED index · `counters.json` unchanged. Single writer: `core/backlog.py`.
  Register/adjust in `config/store-registry.json`.

## API contract
- UNCHANGED public API (`core/backlog.py`). Storage layout is an implementation detail - all consumers
  already go through the API.

## Edge cases & errors
- Migration idempotent + re-runnable; backup before write; abort on hash mismatch.
- Concurrency: keep the `.lock` + atomic `os.replace`; index regeneration inside the same lock.
- Partial migration -> read-fallback covers mixed state.

## Dependencies & links
- Related (not blocking): BI-0168 (static index.html, completed), BI-0153 (log conventions, completed).
- Consistency reference: per-item `products/intake/*/items.jsonl` already use the jsonl pattern.

## Open questions
- Do Stage 1 now and Stage 2 later, or both together?
- Journal granularity: full body before/after, or a diff/hash to keep files small?
- Keep `open.json` as the derived index, or introduce a separate `index.json`?

## Verification / test plan
- Migration test: item count + content hashes equal before/after; re-run is a no-op.
- Round-trip test: add/update/close an item -> per-item file + journal + derived index all correct.
- Consumer regression: `python -m core.backlog`, `current views.py index.html`, dashboard API unchanged.
- Gates: `compileall` + `wired_audit` green; store-registry updated.

dashboard_impact.reason: Internal storage refactor; all consumers use the backlog API, so no dashboard/UI change.

_note: core/backlog.py now: items/<ID>.json = TRUTH; open.json/closed.json = DERIVED lean index (id/status/one-liner/dates, no body/links); history/<ID>.jsonl = content journal (status + field diffs). New API: list_items/get/history/index_view/archive/delete + migrate_scope. Bypasses fixed: core/views.py:_all_backlog_items + dashboard/api/app.py:backlog_history now use the API. Migrated 316 items (product_forge=179, ProductForge-Dashboard=136, test-project=1) - counts MATCH; idempotent. scripts/dev/migrate_backlog_storage.py. Registered items/ + history/ in store-registry + allow glob. Round-trip verified (add/update/complete/archive/delete + journal diff). Gate: compileall=0, wired_audit=0.
